proof: Two same-identity measurements yield the same legacy support/contradiction summary yet different integrated first-return support mass under the same existing millimetre quantization. Keeping other metadata equal, no function of that summary can recover both masses. This proves insufficiency for that nontrivial soft-measurement kernel, not impossibility of all probabilistic models.
limitations: Uniform within-quantization-cell phase is the existing M1 discretization approximation; it is not a learned depth-noise law. The example is an analytic counterexample, not GT evidence or an executed dataset trial. No probability of whole-object absence is inferred from support mass alone.
required_information: Per-ray residual/association intervals or an equivalent probability sufficient statistic, with shared ray IDs to preserve dependencies. P18 is the listed measurement-classification gate; adding arbitrary false-positive rates at P12 is not permitted.
